text:
Maria (CS): FYI — customer ACME (acct: acme-42) opened an urgent ticket. They report repeated 429s and 2-3x tail-latency spikes from their Dedicated pool during nightly embedding batches over the last 90m. They say one node shows GPU at ~95% while others are under 20%.

Priya (Support-Eng): Can you paste the pool id and any request ids? Also did they change model configs or MIG profile yesterday?

Maria (CS): pool_id: dedicated-pool-eu-west-7. They did a MIG reconfiguration last night to mix 7g + 2g slices for different teams. Sample error from their client:
```
{"error":"429 Too Many Requests","request_id":"r-0a1b2c3d","latency_ms":1240}
```
They also provided an ops snapshot (I'll attach).

Devon (Infra): Quick triage checklist:
- check node GPU util: `kubectl top nodes` and `nvidia-smi` on that node
- dcgm/dmon snapshots for GPU mem/copy/encoders
- check scheduler logs for pending pods and scale events
- confirm MIG partitioning (`nvidia-smi mig -lgci`)

Kevin (SRE): Also confirm autoscaler didn't hit max capacity. If autoscaler refused to scale because of quotas or taints that would explain fallback throttles.

ops-bot: autoscaler: no scale-up events detected for pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-7 between 2025-05-30T01:00Z and 2025-05-30T03:00Z. Max nodes configured: 12, current nodes: 10.

Priya (Support-Eng): Maria — can you run the customer's repro (they provided a small load script) against a test replica of the pool so we can observe? They gave these steps:
```bash
# repro: parallel embedding calls
for i in {1..150}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/acme-embed/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"lorem ipsum"}' &\
done
wait
```

Maria (CS): Running now against a staging node that mirrors their MIG setup.

Sam (Eng-ML): A couple of notes from runtime side: when you mix MIG slices (e.g., 7g + 2g) on the same physical GPU, one heavy process on a 7g slice can still cause L2/cache and PCIe interference for other slices depending on kernel scheduling and driver behavior. Also some workloads trigger GPU clocks/boost which can affect thermal/power budgets and cause throttling. Not a pure 'MIG isolation' guarantee in those mixed configs.

Devon (Infra): If autoscaler can't add nodes because of quota, we should fallback to shedding or queueing; but we're seeing 429s instead of queued tokens. That means the serving layer decided to reject instead of stall. Need to check the serving policy for that pool.

Maria (CS): Observed on staging: around iteration ~40 we hit 429s and one node shows sustained 96% GPU utilization. Other nodes are 12-18%. Logs from the node:
```
[2025-05-30T02:11:12Z] model-server: dropping request, queue_full=128, inflight=130
[2025-05-30T02:11:12Z] nvidia-smi: GPU 0 Util 96%, Mem 10.2Gi/11Gi
[2025-05-30T02:11:13Z] dcgm: memory_copy_bw drop detected, encoder spikes
```

Kevin (SRE): Can you collect dcgm diagnostics and GPU metrics (sm, mem_bw, power) and attach them to the ticket? Also check kernel logs for thermal throttling: `dmesg | grep -i thermal`

Maria (CS): Attached dcgm snapshots and `dmesg`. Didn't see obvious thermal errors tho.

Sam (Eng-ML): Short-term mitigations we can propose to customer:
- move heavy nightly batch jobs to a dedicated, non-shared node (no MIG sharing)
- adjust autoscaler policy to be more aggressive (lower CPU/GPU thresholds) or bump max nodes
- set kube scheduling to avoid colocation of heavy embed jobs on same host (nodeAffinity/taints)

Devon (Infra): Long-term: consider enforcing homogenous MIG configs per node (all slices same profile) or use full-GPU reservations for production critical workloads. Also we should add an autoscaler check to detect asymmetric GPU saturation across a pool and trigger proactive scale-up.

Priya (Support-Eng): I'll open an internal escalation and tag eng-runtime. Action items for us now:
1) collect dcgm + nvidia-smi + pod allocation traces (done, attached)
2) repro on staging and record perf traces (Maria running)
3) propose quick mitigation to customer (move nightly to isolated node)
4) escalate to eng-runtime for root cause and scheduler changes

Priya (Support-Eng): Created ticket INC-2026 and assigned to eng-runtime. Attachments: dcgm.tar.gz, dmesg.log, staging-repro-trace.log.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance window on pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-7 at 2025-05-31T02:00Z — rolling kernel/driver bump.

Maria (CS): Customer is OK with moving the batch job to an isolated node. They asked if there will be any billing impacts if we create an isolated node for them for 24 hours.

Kevin (SRE): Billing: creating a temporary dedicated node will be billed as reserved usage if we allocate from Dedicated capacity. We can offer a one-off credit for their outage window; coordinate with finance.

Sam (Eng-ML): One more data point — MIG + MPS don't mix well. If someone enabled MPS on that host in the past it could leave persistent scheduling artifacts. Check `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` processes.

Devon (Infra): I'm going to run a targeted experiment: reproduce load with and without mixing MIG profiles on same GPU, and with our kernel+driver branch to see if the observed memory-bandwidth contention is driver-related. Will report back in ~3 hours.

Maria (CS): Thanks everyone — I'll tell the customer we have a plan: 1) move batch to isolated node tomorrow 09:00 UTC, 2) ENG will run root-cause experiments, 3) we'll follow up with timeline and any credit. :thumbsup:

Priya (Support-Eng): tagging @Sam @Devon @Kevin — please post initial findings in INC-2026.

Maria (CS): Closing the customer-facing loop now. Will update this thread with incident/ticket number when eng-runtime posts RCA.

[thread-end]
